meta.title: SolarArc — Clean energy and food from saline land
meta.description: SolarArc: solar panels on raised steel arches over saline land. Clean energy on top, food underneath. CECECO Clean Energy Hackathon 2027.

hero.title: Turning dead saline land into clean energy and food
hero.subtitle: Energy on top. An oasis below.
hero.lead: SolarArc raises solar panels on {{height}} m steel arches over salt-damaged land. The same hectare produces clean electricity above and crops below, while the shade slows evaporation and helps the soil recover.

problem.title: Good land is turning white with salt
problem.lead: Azerbaijan has a lot of sun and a lot of saline land. Today, neither is used well.

saline.title: Saline land
saline.body: Kura-Araz, Mil-Mugan and Absheron have hundreds of thousands of hectares of saline soil. In +40 °C summers irrigation water evaporates, the salt stays in the topsoil, crops fail and farmers abandon the land.

singleUse.title: Classic solar uses land for only one thing
singleUse.body: Conventional ground-mounted plants produce electricity and nothing else. The land underneath gives no food and is never restored.

diagram.alt: Diagram: the hot sun evaporates water from the soil surface, water rises and leaves a white salt layer in the topsoil, and the plant dries out.
diagram.caption: How salt rises: every time water evaporates from bare soil, the salt it carried stays behind near the surface.

solution.title: How SolarArc works
solution.lead: One structure, three jobs: produce energy, grow food and bring saline soil back to life. Tap the numbers to explore the cross-section.

diagram.alt: Cross-section of a SolarArc bay: a steel arch with curved solar panels on top, crops and drip lines underneath, soil layers and a ground cooling channel below. East is on the right, West on the left.

arch.title: Raised steel arch ({{height}} m)
arch.body: Coated steel lifts the panels high enough for people and small machines to work underneath. The open lattice lets wind pass through instead of pushing against a solid wall.

layout.title: Curved East–West panel layout
layout.body: Panels follow the curve of the arch, so they face different directions. East-facing panels catch the morning sun, West-facing panels the evening sun — output is spread across the day, not only around midday.

shade.title: Shade
shade.body: Partial shade under the arch lowers soil temperature and reduces evaporation, so less salt is pulled up to the surface.

drip.title: Drip irrigation + EC sensors
drip.body: Electrical conductivity (EC) sensors track soil salinity. Drip lines deliver water exactly where it is needed and, when required, flush salt down below the root zone.

cooling.title: Ground cooling channel
cooling.body: A channel in the ground supplies cooler air under the arch, which should help the panels run cooler. This idea is still being tested on the prototype.

crops.title: Crops underneath
crops.body: We choose crops that like partial shade, tolerate some salinity and sell at a premium — from mushrooms in the darkest zone to sweet cherry tomatoes.

energy.title: Energy
energy.body: Clean electricity from the panels, spread across morning, midday and evening.

food.title: Food
food.body: Shade- and salt-tolerant premium crops grown on land that produced nothing before.

soil.title: Soil restoration
soil.body: Shade and controlled drip irrigation keep salt down, so the land can gradually recover.

interior.alt: Concept visualization: inside a long arched tunnel whose roof is made of solar panels. Two farmers tend rows of tomatoes and climbing cucumbers; cabbages grow in raised beds with drip-irrigation lines along the ground.
interior.caption: Inside the arch: crops growing under the solar roof. Concept visualization.

aerial.alt: Concept visualization: aerial view of four parallel solar-panel arches on a farm, with tomatoes and cabbages growing in beds underneath, open fields around them and farm buildings and tractors in the background.
aerial.caption: A SolarArc farm from above. Concept visualization.

video.label: Concept video: a drone flies over rows of arches roofed entirely with solar panels, standing on white salt-crusted land, with green crops growing in the shade underneath.
video.caption: SolarArc in motion: the solar roof covers the whole garden. Concept visualization.

prototype.title: A working prototype, not just a drawing.
prototype.lead: We built a tabletop model of the arch to test the idea with real sunlight and real measurements.

photo.alt: The SolarArc tabletop prototype: a white curved arch on two feet, its top covered with a row of small solar cells, with the measurement controller board (red LED lit) standing underneath.
photo.caption: The working tabletop prototype with its on-board controller.

drawing.alt: Technical drawing, Fig. 1 — East–West section of the solar arch: a steel truss arch, ten solar panels mounted on the west interior of the arch, and a tilted ground mirror outside the east side reflecting morning sunlight onto the panels.
drawing.caption: Fig. 1 — East–West section of the arch (morning-corrected design). Click to enlarge.

points.realtime: The model generates electricity in real time from sunlight or a lamp.
points.controller: An on-board controller measures voltage, current and power — the data feeds the dashboard below.

sim.title: Move the sun, compare the curves
sim.lead: Drag the time of day and switch the season. Compare a curved SolarArc with the same number of flat panels tilted 30° to the South.

view.altUp: At {{time}} the sun is {{elevation}}° above the horizon (azimuth {{azimuth}}°). Arch panels are coloured by how much light each one receives.
view.altDown: At {{time}} the sun is below the horizon. No panel produces power.

sim.chartTitle: Power over the day (flat-panel summer peak = 100)
sim.chartAlt: Line chart of power over the day for SolarArc and a flat panel. The selected time is marked with a vertical line.

stats.caption: Daily results, {{season}}
stats.shoulder: Share of energy before 10:00 and after 16:00
stats.units: Relative units: power is scaled so the flat-panel summer peak = 100; energy = power × hours.

sim.takeaway: The arch starts earlier and keeps going later, so a bigger share of its energy comes in the morning and evening. The flat south-facing panel has a higher midday peak and, in this model, more total energy per panel — especially in winter. SolarArc's value is the wider curve together with food and soil restoration on the same land.
sim.caption: Simplified geometric model for illustration. Real performance is being measured on the prototype.

dashboard.title: Live dashboard
dashboard.lead: Readings from the prototype's on-board controller. When the prototype isn't connected, the dashboard shows realistic demo data.
dashboard.chartAlt: Area chart of the last {{count}} power readings.

crops.title: What grows in the shade
crops.lead: Crops chosen for partial shade, tolerance to salinity and a strong market price.

mushrooms.name: Mushrooms
mushrooms.note: Grow in the darkest, coolest zone.

strawberry.name: Strawberry
strawberry.note: High-value berry that welcomes shade in hot summers.

spinach.name: Spinach
spinach.note: Fast leafy crop — one of the first harvests.

garlic.name: Garlic
garlic.note: Hardy crop that stores well and fills the cooler season.

microgreensBasil.name: Microgreens + basil
microgreensBasil.note: Short growing cycles, high value per square metre.

premium.title: Saline Premium
premium.body: Under mild, controlled salt stress, tomatoes accumulate more sugar. On SolarArc land, sweetness is a selling point, not a defect.

chart.alt: Bar chart on {{area}} ha: capacity — SolarArc {{sMw}} MW, classic solar {{cMw}} MW; annual generation — SolarArc {{sGwh}} GWh, classic solar {{cGwh}} GWh.

roadmap.title: From one arch to a region
roadmap.lead: We start small, measure everything, then scale.

s1.what: Soil testing, EC mapping, 1 ha pilot arch built.

s2.what: Pilot testing, first mushroom and spinach harvest, salinity data.

s3.what: Scale to 10 ha, all crops planted.

s5.what: 100 ha cluster → ECO region (Türkiye, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Pakistan).

partners.title: Who we're looking for
partners.lead: SolarArc needs partners on the ground, on the grid and in the field.

land.title: Land partner
land.body: Owners or managers of saline plots ready for a pilot.

grid.title: Energy / grid partner
grid.body: Grid connection, power purchase and technical support.

investor.title: Investor
investor.body: Funding for the 1 ha pilot and the 10 ha scale-up.
